card.title: Bandwidth and propagation of electromagnetic waves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Bandwidth is the frequency width a signal needs. Ground waves follow the Earth at lower frequencies, sky waves can bounce from the ionosphere, and space waves travel in line of sight. The radio horizon of a mast of height h is about the square root of 2 R h.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Take R = 6400 km unless the question gives another radius.  ·  Night-time ionosphere conditions change the sky-wave range.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a signal or a channel occupies. A wider message, such as television, needs a wider channel than speech. Two stations must be separated by at least their bandwidths or they overlap.  ·  A ground wave travels along the surface of the Earth. The ground absorbs more energy at higher frequency, so ground-wave broadcast is used for the lower radio frequencies and does not reach around the world.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Bandwidth  ·  Ground wave  ·  Sky wave  ·  Space wave

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Bandwidth is the spread of frequencies used.  ·  Ground waves follow the Earth.  ·  Sky waves reflect from the ionosphere.  ·  Space waves travel in line of sight.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What does a higher mast do to the radio horizon?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A transmitting antenna is 100 m above the Earth. Take R = 6.40 × 10^6 m. Estimate the radio-horizon distance with √(2 R h).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Television typically uses → B  ·  A sky wave can be returned by → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A sky wave is sent upward and can be returned by the ionosphere. That is how short-wave radio crosses long distances. The ionosphere is not a metal mirror at every frequency: above a critical frequency the wave passes through.  ·  A space wave travels in a straight line from a high transmitting antenna to the receiver. Television and FM use it. The Earth's curve limits the range to a little beyond the geometric horizon.  ·  For an antenna at height h above a spherical Earth of radius R, the horizon distance is about √(2 R h) when h is much smaller than R. A higher mast sees farther.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ..  ·  Bandwidth is not the carrier frequency.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A sky wave is not guaranteed at every frequency.  ·  A space wave does not follow the ground.  ·  The horizon formula uses the radius of the Earth, not the height alone.
